title: What a server says when it cannot do what was asked

expect.why: A session that was never created is absent, not forbidden — the caller is authorized, the thing is not there.
The client library must not report a 404 as success; a caller would read the error body as a session.
The message names what was asked for. Pinned exactly because an operator greps for it, and because a port that echoes the id differently is a port with a different escaping story.
A path in no route table is absent.
The framework default in the reference. Recorded so a port that answers its own framework's wording shows up here rather than in a consumer's error dialog.
A known path with an unknown method is not a 404: the difference is what tells a client to stop retrying versus to fix the verb.
Same reasoning as the 404 wording — the reference's answer, pinned so a divergence is visible.
Authentication is decided before existence. Answering 404 to an anonymous caller would let anyone enumerate which session ids exist.
The same refusal as any other unauthenticated request — it must not leak that the path was routable.
